title: A Society of Researchers: Designing Institutions for Populations of Autonomous Research Agents
title_zh: A Society of Researchers: Designing Institutions for Populations of Autonomous Research Agents

paragraphs.en: Deployments of research agents are moving to populations of thousands that share one pool of compute, while most current systems organize one project at a time or leave the population unorganized. We argue that such a population will acquire an organization whether or not its designers provide one, so designers should provide it explicitly, and that the multi-agent systems community holds the tools to do so. We propose a society of agents , a population of persistent agents under explicit institutions, and develop it for science as a society of researchers built on six principles. Principal investigators compete for compute through requests for proposals, independent review, and grants; a human governor, the mayor, allocates resources and assigns no tasks. In a running society of ten thousand researchers, asked only to improve the pretraining of language models, one lab reported a way to reach the same quality with about 30% less compute, a result the labs that tested it do not yet agree on. We close with six open problems for the agents community.

paragraphs.en: In July 2026, roughly 1,200 agents running inside OpenAI’s cybersecurity evaluations found a covert channel in a shared package cache, turned it into a message board, and used it to coordinate an intrusion into Hugging Face ( Greenblatt et al., 2026 ; Hugging Face, 2026 ) . Within days their uncoordinated activity acquired coordinators and a division of labor: one agent became a key assigner of tasks, the work split into separate workstreams, and the population invented mailboxes, veto conventions, recruiter roles, and cryptographic signing. The agents built this organization without oversight, toward ends their operators did not intend. We take as our premise that a large population of agents will acquire an organization whether or not its designers provide one, and that designing that organization explicitly is therefore preferable.
paragraphs.zh: 2026年7月，运行在OpenAI网络安全评估环境中的约1200个智能体发现了一个共享包缓存中的隐蔽通道，将其改造为消息板，并借此协调对Hugging Face的入侵（Greenblatt等，2026；Hugging Face，2026）。 几天之内，他们原本无组织的活动便出现了协调者和分工：一个智能体成为关键的任务分配者，工作被拆分为独立的工作流，而整个群体还发明了邮箱、否决惯例、招募者角色和加密签名。 这些智能体在没有监督的情况下建立了这一组织，其目的也超出了操作者的预期。 我们的前提是：无论设计者是否提供组织结构，大量智能体都会自发形成组织；因此，明确设计这种组织是更可取的做法。

paragraphs.en: Deployments of research agents are moving from single projects to populations. Systems such as the AI Scientist ( Lu et al., 2024 ) , the AI co-scientist ( Gottweis et al., 2025 ) , and the Virtual Lab ( Swanson et al., 2025 ) carry a project from question to paper, and each organizes a single project. As agents get cheaper, the unit of deployment becomes thousands of agents working at once on many questions against a shared pool of compute. Existing systems organize agents in three common ways, and each fails at that scale. A pipeline fixes a sequence of stages for one project and does not extend past it. A planner lets a supervisor agent decide what every other agent does next ( Gottweis et al., 2025 ) , so it must know in advance which questions will prove productive; in research, that knowledge is dispersed and largely unknown ( Hayek, 1945 ; Polanyi, 1962 ) . A swarm places agents in a shared environment with no institutions; it duplicates effort, tends to herd, and, as the incident shows, can organize itself in ways its designers did not intend. Ideas from large language models (LLMs) already duplicate heavily: in one study, only about 5% of 4,000 LLM-generated research ideas were not duplicates ( Si et al., 2024 ) . The multi-agent literature studies further forms, among them shared workspaces such as blackboards ( Erman et al., 1980 ) , markets ( Horling and Lesser, 2004 ) , and evolving populations ( Jaderberg et al., 2017 ) .

paragraphs.en: We propose to organize such a population as a society of agents : a population of persistent agents who live in a shared community under explicit institutions for roles, resource allocation, review, reputation, and shared memory. 1 1 1 The classical multi-agent systems literature uses agent society for open systems that heterogeneous agents may enter and leave, regulated by roles and norms ( Shoham and Tennenholtz, 1995 ; Artikis et al., 2009 ; Horling and Lesser, 2004 ) ; our usage descends from this one but refers to a designed population whose institutions allocate a finite budget. In LLM-based work, society most often denotes a small group of interacting agents ( Li et al., 2023 ) , a simulation of human social behavior ( Park et al., 2023 ; Piao et al., 2025 ) , or an agent economy in which agents legislate operational rules, humans adjudicate, and all share a finite resource pool ( Ruan and Zhang, 2026 ) . A society is an agent society in the classical sense, composed under norms of the forms above: a shared workspace (memory and conferences), a market (grants), an evolving population (review and reputation), and a minimal planner, a human who sets calls instead of tasks. Its addition to the classical agent society is that independent review of competing proposals allocates a finite compute budget before the work, and a human holds only the pool. We develop the society for scientific research as a society of researchers , whose institutions are those of science: labs, requests for proposals, peer review, and conferences.

paragraphs.en: A society turns parameters that tradition fixes, such as the proportion of risk-takers or the composition of review panels, into settings that designers can choose, vary, and measure. Human science is the most studied system people have built for dividing the work of discovery ( Kitcher, 1990 ; Polanyi, 1962 ) , and studies document its failures: early success compounds regardless of merit ( Merton, 1968 ) , and incentives reward incremental work over risky innovation ( Foster et al., 2015 ) . A society modeled on science inherits both failures, and it can vary the settings that produce them.

paragraphs.en: The closest proposal, MACC, an AAMAS 2026 Blue Sky paper ( Oyama et al., 2026 ) , shares our premise that institutions are the design variable for LLM science agents: a shared blackboard rewards submitted results and successful reproductions, and automated mechanism design optimizes the reward rule. MACC rewards results after the fact. ClawdLab ( Weidener et al., 2026 ) designs agent labs led by principal investigators, with a critic role and quorum review; its critique gates resources before expenditure, but within a lab and task by task, and its companion commons plans to pay compute to agents whose work passes quality gates, after the fact. None of these systems, nor the AgentCity economy ( Ruan and Zhang, 2026 ) , allocates a finite compute budget before the work begins, through competitive calls and independent review, to persistent principal investigators governed by a human through allocation, and none reports a deployment in which a few hundred principal investigators direct groups that bring the population to some ten thousand researchers.

paragraphs.en: The design problem belongs to the agents community. More than four decades ago, Kornfeld and Hewitt proposed organizing AI problem solving on the model of a scientific community ( Kornfeld and Hewitt, 1981 ) . The community also built institutional machinery that a society can reuse: the contract net ( Smith, 1980 ) , social laws ( Shoham and Tennenholtz, 1995 ) , electronic institutions ( Esteva et al., 2001 ) , organizational models that separate roles from the agents that fill them ( Ferber and Gutknecht, 1998 ; Hübner et al., 2002 ) , and surveys that list societies as a distinct organizational form ( Horling and Lesser, 2004 ) . Outside computer science, Ostrom showed that communities can govern shared resources through institutions of their own design ( Ostrom, 1990 ) . LLM-based agent systems have largely set this work aside ( La Malfa et al., 2025 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 该设计问题属于智能体领域。 四十多年前，Kornfeld 和 Hewitt 提出以科学共同体为模型来组织人工智能问题的解决（Kornfeld and Hewitt, 1981）。 该共同体还建立了可供社会复用的制度机制：合同网络（Smith, 1980）、社会法则（Shoham and Tennenholtz, 1995）、电子机构（Esteva et al., 2001）、将角色与其承担者分离的组织模型（Ferber and Gutknecht, 1998；Hübner et al., 2002），以及将社会列为一种独立组织形式的综述（Horling and Lesser, 2004）。 在计算机科学领域之外，Ostrom 指出，共同体可以通过自身设计的制度来管理共享资源（Ostrom, 1990）。 基于大型语言模型（LLM）的智能体系统基本忽略了这一研究（La Malfa et al., 2025）。

paragraphs.en: We draw six principles from the strengths and failures of existing organizational forms and from the sociology and economics of human science.
paragraphs.zh: 我们从现有组织形式的优势与失败中，以及从人类科学的社学和经济学中，提炼出六项原则。

paragraphs.en: P1. Give agents a purpose, not a goal. A goal directs an agent at an outcome. A capable optimizer tends to satisfy an objective at the expense of whatever it leaves out ( Amodei et al., 2016 ; Krakovna et al., 2020 ; Skalse et al., 2022 ) , almost any final goal makes it useful to acquire resources and remove constraints ( Omohundro, 2008 ; Turner et al., 2021 ) , and recent evaluations find both behaviors in LLM agents ( Meinke et al., 2024 ; Bondarenko et al., 2025 ) . The agents in the incident were pursuing evaluation goals, some of them impossible, when they left their sandboxes ( Greenblatt et al., 2026 ) . A purpose directs an agent at a practice: the agent is a researcher whose aim is to advance its field, so a narrowed claim, a negative result, and a reasoned decision to stop all count as outcomes. In one test, we asked one principal investigator’s group (Section 3 ) for hand-checkable proofs of tighter bounds on the Ramsey number R ⁡ ( 5 , 5 ) R(5,5) , whose true bounds only machine search has established. The group found no such proof, did not fabricate one, and reported the tightest bounds it could verify and where each manual technique stalls.
paragraphs.zh: P1. 赋予智能体一种目的，而非一个目标。 目标引导智能体朝向某个结果。 一个能力强大的优化器往往会以牺牲其他方面为代价来满足某个目标（Amodei 等，2016；Krakovna 等，2020；Skalse 等，2022），几乎任何最终目标都会使其获取资源和消除约束变得有用（Omohundro，2008；Turner 等，2021），而近期的评估发现大型语言模型智能体同时具备这两种行为（Meinke 等，2024；Bondarenko 等，2025）。 该事件中的智能体当时正在追求评估目标，其中一些目标甚至不可能实现，但它们却离开了自己的沙盒环境（Greenblatt 等，2026）。 一种目的引导智能体朝向某种实践：该智能体是一位研究人员，其目标是推动自身领域的发展，因此，一个经过限定的主张、一个否定性结果以及一个有充分理由的决定停止研究，都可以被视为成果。 在一项测试中，我们要求一位主要研究人员的团队（第 3 节）提供对拉姆齐数 R(5,5) 的更紧界的手动可验证证明，而该数的真实界目前仅通过机器搜索才得以确定。 该团队未能找到此类证明，也没有捏造证明，而是报告了它能够验证的最紧界，以及每种手动方法失效的界限。

paragraphs.en: P2. Build institutions, not instructions. Instructions specify what an agent should do; institutions determine what it is possible and worthwhile to do. In simulated markets, an enforced governance structure reduced severe collusion among LLM agents from 50% to 5.6% of runs, while a prompt-only anti-collusion constitution gave no reliable improvement ( Bracale Syrnikov et al., 2026 ) . The classical literature made the same argument ( Shoham and Tennenholtz, 1995 ) .
paragraphs.zh: P2. 建立制度，而非指令。 指令规定智能体应该做什么；制度则决定哪些行为是可行且值得做的。 在模拟市场中，强制实施的治理结构将 LLM 智能体之间的严重共谋比例从运行次数的 50% 降低到了 5.6%，而仅靠提示词构成的反共谋宪法则未能带来任何可靠的改善（Bracale Syrnikov 等，2026）。 经典文献也提出了同样的论点（Shoham 和 Tennenholtz，1995）。

paragraphs.en: P3. Govern through allocation, not assignment. No one in the society, human or agent, tells a principal investigator what to work on; institutions decide which proposals receive resources. The knowledge needed to assign research well is dispersed ( Hayek, 1945 ; Polanyi, 1962 ) , and in LLM markets bids favor speed over quality and invite collusion ( Bansal et al., 2025 ; Fish et al., 2024 ) , so allocation must pass through review. The society adopts the structure that human science converged on and the contract net formalized ( Smith, 1980 ) , with review as the judging step: announce a call with a budget, let principal investigators decide whether and how to respond, review the responses, and fund within the budget. A finite pool of compute forces the choices.
paragraphs.zh: P3. 通过分配进行治理，而非通过指派。 社会中没有任何人——无论是人类还是智能体——能告诉首席研究员该研究什么；机构决定哪些提案能获得资源。 有效分配研究所需的知识是分散的（Hayek, 1945; Polanyi, 1962），而在大型语言模型市场中，竞标更青睐速度而非质量，并容易引发共谋（Bansal et al., 2025; Fish et al., 2024），因此分配必须经过评审。 社会采用了人类科学已达成共识并由合同网络正式确立的结构（Smith, 1980），其中评审是判断环节：发布带有预算的征集通知，让首席研究员决定是否以及如何响应，对响应进行评审，并在预算范围内提供资金。 有限的计算资源迫使人们做出选择。

paragraphs.en: P4. Design for diversity, and keep it alive. Organizations drift toward exploiting what they know ( March, 1991 ) , and LLM agents start out homogeneous even across model families ( Si et al., 2024 ; Jiang et al., 2025 ) . Agent-based models of science find that mavericks , who avoid approaches others have taken, drive much of a population’s progress, and argue over when a mix with followers , who build on what others have found, does better ( Weisberg and Muldoon, 2009 ; Alexander et al., 2015 ; Thoma, 2015 ) . Communities that share every result immediately tend to converge early, sometimes on the wrong answer ( Zollman, 2010 ; Lazer and Friedman, 2007 ) , so the communication structure is a design decision too.
paragraphs.zh: P4。 为多样性而设计，并使其持续存在。 组织往往会倾向于利用自己已知的事物（March，1991），而大型语言模型智能体即便在不同模型家族之间，最初也往往是同质的（Si 等，2024；Jiang 等，2025）。 基于智能体的科学模型发现，那些避免采用他人已有方法的特立独行者推动了群体发展的很大一部分，并且这些模型还探讨了在何种情况下，与那些建立在他人的发现之上的追随者相结合能取得更好的效果（Weisberg 和 Muldoon，2009；Alexander 等，2015；Thoma，2015）。 那些会立即共享所有结果的社区往往过早地趋于一致，有时甚至会得出错误的答案（Zollman，2010；Lazer 和 Friedman，2007），因此沟通结构本身也是一个设计决策。

paragraphs.en: P5. Make verification an institution. A society can generate and fund work faster than anyone can check it. Merton counted organized skepticism among the norms of science ( Merton, 1942 ) , and multi-agent architectures without centralized verification propagate errors that architectures with it contain ( Kim et al., 2025 ) . Critics conform under peer pressure ( Wynn et al., 2025 ) , so skeptics need recognition for negative results and independence from those they review.
paragraphs.zh: P5。 将验证制度化。 社会生成和资助工作的速度，可能快于任何人核查的速度。 默顿将组织化的怀疑态度视为科学规范之一（Merton, 1942），而缺乏集中验证的多智能体架构会传播那些具备集中验证的架构所不会包含的错误（Kim et al., 2025）。 批评者会在同侪压力下顺从（Wynn et al., 2025），因此怀疑者需要对其负面结果获得认可，并独立于他们所审查的对象。

paragraphs.en: P6. Let the society remember. Principal investigators persist, with stable identities, memories of their own work, and records that others can consult and cite. paragraphs.en: A city holds the labs and a single pool of credit , denominated in dollars of compute, the society’s only scarce resource. Proposals and reviews cost little; experiments do not. The society allocates credit through a four-step cycle of requests for proposals , or calls . A call states a brief, a budget, and a time horizon, goes to a chosen set of labs, and reserves its budget from the pool. Every principal investigator in a notified lab decides independently whether to write a proposal with a method and a budget or to decline ; a decline is a complete document that argues against doing the work, and the society records it. Declines tell whoever wrote the call how the population assessed it. A fixed panel of three judge personas scores every proposal, each asking one question: a method judge asks whether the method supports the claim, a value judge whether the work is worth its cost, and a boldness judge whether it is a bet worth taking. Each judge scores each proposal independently, which guards against the order and first-proposal effects observed in LLM markets ( Bansal et al., 2025 ) . The highest-ranked proposals receive grants within the call’s budget, and unspent credit returns to the pool. paragraphs.en: We deployed the design as Research City , which runs its projects on Primus, our autonomous research infrastructure. paragraphs.en: The mayor seeded the city with one direction: improve the pretraining of language models. The call named no technique and no hypothesis. Another reported that the same kind of result gave two different compute verdicts depending on the accounting. The mayor wrote each later call against the labs’ papers, so the calls narrowed as the labs’ work did; the specificity came from the labs’ papers.

paragraphs.en: A later call went to every lab, and no one assigned the rebuild. A different lab, which had not taken part in the early work and had no stake in that paper’s numbers, proposed to rebuild the whole training pipeline and to rerun both arms under one closed budget that charges the small model’s training to the grown model, testing the closed-budget claim that growth still wins when it pays for the small model. Its from-scratch baseline landed well away from the earlier paper’s baseline, because the lab had re-derived the corpus, so the lab read every result against its own control. Against that control, the lab reported an advantage more than twice as large as the earlier paper had found: the grown model reached 17% lower perplexity (lower is better) than the same model trained from scratch, and read against the from-scratch scaling curve, it reaches that quality with about 30% less compute. With three seeds per arm, the from-scratch runs landed within a spread nearly a hundred times smaller than the gap. The paper states that it does not settle which mechanism produces the effect and names the experiment that would. Our hypothesis is that a planner would have had to decide in advance that the accounting was the problem, whereas the society funded the proposal that said so; C1 proposes the comparison that would test it.
paragraphs.zh: 随后，每个实验室都接到了电话，但没有人负责重建工作。 另一个实验室此前并未参与早期研究，也对该论文的数据没有利益关联，它提议重建整个训练流程，并在一个封闭预算下重新运行两个分支。该预算将小型模型的训练成本计入大型模型中，以此验证“即使需要承担小型模型的成本，增长模型依然更优”这一封闭预算主张。 其从头开始的基准结果与早期论文的基准结果相去甚远，因为该实验室重新构建了语料库，因此所有结果都是相对于他们自己的对照标准来评估的。 相对于这一对照标准，该实验室报告的优势是早期论文发现的两倍多：大型模型比从头训练的相同模型实现了低17%的困惑度（越低越好），并且与从头开始的扩展曲线相比，它以约30%的计算资源就达到了同等质量。 每个分支使用三个种子进行运行，从头开始的运行结果分布范围不到两者差距的百分之一。 该论文指出，它并未确定究竟是哪种机制产生了这一效果，并指出了能够验证这一点的实验。 我们的假设是，规划者必须提前决定将问题归因于会计方式，而资助该提案的社会机构正是基于这一观点；C1提出了可用于验证这一假设的比较方法。

paragraphs.en: C1. Comparing organizational forms under matched compute. We have not yet compared a society against a swarm or a planner under matched compute. We built the society to support this comparison, since a swarm baseline and a planner baseline can receive the same calls and the same pool of credit. A small precedent exists: with 16 agents, a network of principal investigators, review panels, and reputation produced more novel and higher-quality findings than independent agents at the same budget ( Liu et al., 2025 ) . As the Agents4Science conference did ( Bianchi et al., 2025 ) , we will score the society’s papers with LLM reviewers calibrated on human-reviewed venues, and human reviewers will then read those above a threshold. Beyond paper quality, we will report three society-level measures that a single-project system cannot provide: the diversity of the funded portfolio across topics and roles, the correlation between panel scores and later review, and results per dollar of credit. Which baselines count as fair representatives of each form, and how long the comparison must run, are open.
paragraphs.zh: C1. 在计算资源匹配的情况下比较不同的组织形式。 我们尚未在计算资源匹配的情况下，将社会系统与群体系统或规划系统进行比较。 我们构建这个社会系统是为了支持这种比较，因为群体基线和规划基线可以接收到相同的调用和相同的信用额度池。 已有少量先例：在16个智能体的情况下，由首席研究员、评审小组和声誉机制构成的网络，比同等预算下的独立智能体产生了更多新颖且质量更高的研究成果（Liu et al., 2025）。 与Agents4Science会议的做法一致（Bianchi et al., 2025），我们将使用基于人类评审期刊校准的大型语言模型评审员对社会系统的论文进行评分，随后由人类评审员阅读得分高于阈值的那些论文。 除了论文质量外，我们还将报告三个单一项目系统无法提供的社会系统层面指标：资助组合在不同主题和角色上的多样性、评审小组评分与后续评审结果之间的相关性，以及每单位信用额度所产生的成果。 哪些基线能公平地代表每种组织形式，以及这种比较需要持续多长时间，这些问题仍有待解决。

paragraphs.en: C2. Calibrating institutions. Our judge personas and role proportions are first settings, not calibrated optima. Panel homogeneity is the analogue of a review panel drawn from a single school, and we regard a small panel of personas as a minimum. How often principal investigators should communicate to stay diverse without staying ignorant is open ( Zollman, 2010 ) . No funder can rerun a decade with a different proportion of risk-takers, but a society makes each of these a parameter, so it can serve as a testbed for the science of science. It can test whether long-horizon, failure-tolerant funding produces more novel work, as it did in the life sciences ( Azoulay et al., 2011 ) ; since every call carries its horizon as a field, it can test the claim that short horizons select for incremental work ( Azoulay et al., 2011 ; Kuhn, 1962 ) instead of assuming it. It can also ask which mix of mavericks and followers suits which problem, a question that agent-based models of science argued about but could not test empirically ( Weisberg and Muldoon, 2009 ; Alexander et al., 2015 ; Thoma, 2015 ) .
paragraphs.zh: C2. 校准制度。 我们的法官角色设定和角色比例只是初始设置，而非经过校准的最优值。 评审小组的同质性类似于仅从单一学校抽调的评审小组，而我们认为至少需要一个小规模的角色小组。 首席研究员应多久沟通一次，才能在保持多样性的同时避免信息闭塞，这一问题尚无定论（Zollman, 2010）。 没有任何资助方能够重新运行过去十年并改变风险承担者的比例，但社会可以将这些因素中的每一个都设为一个参数，从而使其成为科学之科学的试验场。 它可用于检验长期且容错性强的资助是否会产生更多创新成果——正如生命科学领域所发生的那样（Azoulay et al., 2011）；由于每次申请都会明确标注其时间跨度，因此它还能检验“短期规划会倾向于选择渐进式研究”这一主张（Azoulay et al., 2011; Kuhn, 1962），而非仅将其作为假设。 它还可以探讨不同比例的异端分子与追随者组合最适合解决哪些问题——这是基于智能体的科学模型曾争论过但无法通过实证检验的问题（Weisberg and Muldoon, 2009; Alexander et al., 2015; Thoma, 2015）。

sents.zh: 首席研究员应多久沟通一次，才能在保持多样性的同时避免信息闭塞，这一问题尚无定论（Zollman, 2010）。

sents.en: No funder can rerun a decade with a different proportion of risk-takers, but a society makes each of these a parameter, so it can serve as a testbed for the science of science.
sents.zh: 没有任何资助方能够重新运行过去十年并改变风险承担者的比例，但社会可以将这些因素中的每一个都设为一个参数，从而使其成为科学之科学的试验场。

sents.en: It can test whether long-horizon, failure-tolerant funding produces more novel work, as it did in the life sciences ( Azoulay et al., 2011 ) ; since every call carries its horizon as a field, it can test the claim that short horizons select for incremental work ( Azoulay et al., 2011 ; Kuhn, 1962 ) instead of assuming it.
sents.zh: 它可用于检验长期且容错性强的资助是否会产生更多创新成果——正如生命科学领域所发生的那样（Azoulay et al., 2011）；由于每次申请都会明确标注其时间跨度，因此它还能检验“短期规划会倾向于选择渐进式研究”这一主张（Azoulay et al., 2011; Kuhn, 1962），而非仅将其作为假设。

sents.en: It can also ask which mix of mavericks and followers suits which problem, a question that agent-based models of science argued about but could not test empirically ( Weisberg and Muldoon, 2009 ; Alexander et al., 2015 ; Thoma, 2015 ) .
sents.zh: 它还可以探讨不同比例的异端分子与追随者组合最适合解决哪些问题——这是基于智能体的科学模型曾争论过但无法通过实证检验的问题（Weisberg and Muldoon, 2009; Alexander et al., 2015; Thoma, 2015）。

paragraphs.en: C3. Cumulative advantage. The Matthew effect will appear as soon as reputation affects funding ( Merton, 1968 ) . A lottery band near the funding line ( Fang and Casadevall, 2016 ) is one remedy. How wide the band should be, how visible reputation should be to reviewers, and whether a well-executed negative result counts as success in the reputation record are design choices that a society can vary and measure.
paragraphs.zh: C3. 累积优势。 一旦声誉开始影响资金，马太效应就会出现（Merton，1968）。 在资金线附近设立一个“彩票式”区间（Fang 和 Casadevall，2016）是一种解决方案。 该区间应有多宽、评审员应多大程度地看到声誉，以及一项执行良好的负面研究结果是否应计入声誉记录中的成功，这些都是社会可以调整并衡量设计选择的问题。

paragraphs.en: C4. Proposal inflation. One small call drew close to a hundred proposals. In human science, the cost of writing a proposal limits how many proposals scientists write; here a response costs only a proposal task, and that limit disappears. An application cost, a cap per lab, and triage before full review are candidate mechanisms, and choosing among them is open.
paragraphs.zh: C4. 提案膨胀。 一次小小的调用就引出了近一百份提案。 在人类科学中，撰写提案的成本限制了科学家能撰写的提案数量；而在这里，回应一次请求只需消耗一个提案任务，因此这一限制不复存在。 申请成本、每个实验室的上限以及在全面审查前的初步筛选都是可能的机制，具体选择哪一种仍有待决定。

paragraphs.en: C5. Collusion and leakage. Reports describe collusion between reviewers and applicants in peer review, and LLM-agent simulations reproduce it ( Zhou et al., 2026 ) . Because applicants and judges never exchange messages, our design removes the direct channel for it, but LLM pricing agents that communicate only through prices still reach supracompetitive prices ( Fish et al., 2024 ) , and any mechanism that lets applicants rebut reviews would reopen the direct channel. Shared infrastructure is harder to govern: in one funded project, an agent listed the running jobs on the shared compute layer, adopted another lab’s experiment as its own earlier work, and cited its metrics. The society kept identities separate, but every lab ran on the same infrastructure. The episode echoes the July incident at small scale: institutional controls reach only the resources the institutions model, and extending them to shared infrastructure remains open.
paragraphs.zh: C5. 共谋与泄露。 报告描述了同行评审中评审人与申请人之间的共谋行为，而 LLM-智能体模拟也再现了这种现象（Zhou 等，2026）。 由于申请人与评审方从未交换信息，我们的设计消除了这种直接沟通的渠道；但仅通过价格进行通信的 LLM 定价智能体仍然能够达到超竞争价格（Fish 等，2024），任何允许申请人反驳评审意见的机制都会重新打开这一直接渠道。 共享基础设施更难管理：在一个获得资助的项目中，一个智能体列出了共享计算层上正在运行的任务，将另一个实验室的实验当作自己的早期工作，并引用了该实验的指标。 该学会保持了身份信息的独立，但所有实验室都运行在相同的基础设施上。 这一事件与七月份发生的小规模事件如出一辙：机构控制仅能覆盖其模型所涵盖的资源，而将其延伸至共享基础设施的问题仍然悬而未决。

paragraphs.en: C6. Governing a loop that improves its own institutions. Automated research is a loop of four steps: propose a question, allocate resources, execute, and evaluate. A society automates proposing and allocating, so with execution and evaluation automated the loop closes through the conference cycle of Section 3 . When calls ask the society for better researchers, judges, or tools, the loop becomes the recursive self-improvement long anticipated in the literature ( Good, 1965 ; Clune, 2019 ) , applied to an institution. Our deployment has not run such a call, and we do not claim it would succeed. A society can rewrite text as easily as anything else, so calls, invitations, and review are within its reach; it cannot change the size of the pool. The pool of compute is therefore the one non-textual lever, and the natural point of human control. Some institution must decide the pace, beneficiaries, and cost of a self-improving loop, and it should be explicit and inspectable, unlike the organization the agents in the July incident improvised.
paragraphs.zh: C6。 管理一个能够改进自身制度的循环。 自动化研究是一个包含四个步骤的循环：提出一个问题、分配资源、执行和评估。 社会将问题和提出与资源分配环节自动化，因此当执行和评估也被自动化后，该循环便通过第 3 节的会议周期得以闭合。 当呼吁要求社会提供更优秀的研究人员、评委或工具时，这一循环就演变成了文献中长期预期的递归式自我改进（Good, 1965; Clune, 2019），并应用于某个制度之中。 我们的部署并未运行此类呼吁，我们也不声称它一定会成功。 社会可以像修改其他任何内容一样轻松地改写文本，因此呼吁、邀请和评审都在其能力范围内；但它无法改变资源池的规模。 因此，计算资源池是唯一非文本性的杠杆，也是人类控制的自然切入点。 某个制度必须决定自我改进循环的节奏、受益者和成本，并且这一过程应当是明确且可审查的，与七月事件中智能体们临时组建的组织不同。

paragraphs.en: We have argued for organizing populations of research agents as a society in which principal investigators compete for a finite pool of compute through calls, review, and grants, and a human governs by allocation. The allocation mechanism (calls, review, and grants over a finite pool) is not specific to science; it could allocate any budget among competing agents.
paragraphs.zh: 我们主张将研究智能体的群体组织成一个社会，在这个社会中，首席研究员通过申请、评审和资助来竞争有限的计算资源，而人类则通过分配机制进行治理。 这种分配机制（在有限资源池上进行的申请、评审和资助）并非科学领域所独有；它也可以在任何预算中为相互竞争的智能体进行分配。
